messages:
maria.g: Heads up — ran the quarterly access review export this morning and a small cluster of admin grants look ownerless in prod KMS. attaching quick dump: https://redwood-internal/reports/access-review/6112223333.csv :lock:

jordan: ugh, link looks like the same service-roles we thought we removed 2 months ago. can you paste the IDs?

maria.g: pasted IDs below. most are svcacct-KMS-ops-* and 3 user admins with no last-active within 180d.

```
svcacct-kms-ops-12  project:payments  binding:kms.admin
svcacct-kms-ops-47  project:analytics  binding:kms.admin
user:kevin.j  last_active: 2022-09-01  roles:org-admin
user:anna.p   last_active: 2023-02-14  roles:kms-admin
user:temp-admin-ops last_active: 2021-11-03 roles:super-admin
```

ashley: thanks. risk: these KMS admins can rewrap keys. we should treat as high priority for evidence collection before any removals.

leo: agreed. propose steps: 1) confirm last-use via audit logs, 2) message owners / slack ping, 3) schedule canary removal in staging, 4) remove in prod after 72h.

maria.g: audit log query I ran (elk) — pasted below. shows zero decrypt/re-encrypt events in 9 months for the svcacct-47.

```
index=cloud-logs source=kms action=(Decrypt OR Encrypt OR Rewrap) service_account:svcacct-kms-ops-47 | stats count() by action, date
```

maria.g: result: count=0 between 2023-06-01 and 2024-11-01 :eyes:

jordan: can we automate owner-resolution? last time manual pings stalled. maybe fallback to infra-team for orphan service accounts.

access-sweeper-bot: Automated note: Created task #SEC-1227 to track ownerproof, evidence snapshot, and staged-removal. Assigned to @maria.g. Deadline: 2024-11-15.

ashley: ping @sam-oncall — can you add this to the oncall checklist for the next maintenance window? want to avoid a surprise deploy that reads keys right after prune.

sam-oncall: noted. will add a lock window and watch for errors during the prune. also enable a temporary rate-limitier on KMS for 4h post-change.

leo: for the canary: we'll remove binding on staging first using infra-tooling. command when ready:

```
# example (gcloud-esque)
projects set-iam-policy PROJECT_ID --remove-binding="members:svcacct-kms-ops-47, role:roles/cloudkms.admin"
```

maria.g: timeline proposal: owner ping + evidence collection (48h), escalate to infra if no owner (72h), staging canary (next maintenance), prod prune after 72h successful canary.

jordan: also file a short audit entry in the compliance ledger with the justification and snapshot of audit-log query. keep it reversible.

maria.g: will do that. drafting note now and attaching to SEC-1227.

ashley: small ask — can we add a rule to the access-sweeper to auto-tag service accounts that have had 0 KMS ops in 180d and are flagged as admin? at least label them 'suspect-orphan' so they show up in weekly digest.

access-sweeper-bot: Feature request logged: FR-409 — auto-tag suspect-orphan for KMS admin principals with 180d inactivity. Queue: backlog.

leo: assignable owners: @maria.g (evidence + compliance note), @jordan (remediation plan + infra TODO), @sam-oncall (safety window + post-prune monitoring).

maria.g: I started a short thread to owners list and cc'd infra. pinged iam-team@redwood for final confirmation.

jordan: once we remove, make sure to run a quick smoke test on token issuance path — keys used in session token rotation could break auth flows.

sam-oncall: will run smoke tests and watch the error rate dashboard. my fallback is to reapply binding and raise incident if >0.5% request error spike.

maria.g: creating calendar event for staging canary — ETA 2024-11-10 03:00 UTC. I'll update SEC-1227 with exact commands and rollback steps.

leo: thanks everyone. small follow-up: let's add a periodic lint that warns when user admins haven't logged in in >120d even if they aren't KMS admins. we keep accumulating stale human admins.

ashley: +1. can we use SCIM last_active to automate a weekly report?

maria.g: yep. will add to the FR-409 discussion.

jordan: cool. marking this thread for follow-up. :shipit:

sam-oncall: acknowledged. will post a short post-mortem if anything odd happens during the prune.

access-sweeper-bot: Update: task #SEC-1227 status changed to "in progress".
